items: Pani - Washing aur Soaking ke lie
Tomato - 2 medium size, mixi me chala kar use karein

steps.text: Wash chole twice with water and soak in water with 1/4 tsp meetha soda for 6 hours for good flavor absorption.
Soak 1/2 cup suji in 1 cup water for 5 minutes to soften.
Mix 2 cups maida with 2 tsp namak, 2 tsp cheeni, and 1/2 tsp baking soda or meetha soda.
Squeeze out extra water from soaked suji and mix it with the maida mixture.
Add 1-2 tsp dahi to the flour mixture to make dough, adjust water if needed to keep dough tight and not too soft.
Knead the dough for 7 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Add 1 tbsp oil to the dough and knead for another 3-4 minutes to incorporate oil and enhance elasticity.
Coat the dough with 1 tbsp oil and cover with cloth and lid, then let it rest and ferment for 6 hours for best results, minimum 30 minutes acceptable.
Grind 2 medium sized onions and 1 tbsp anardana in a mixer without adding water to make a paste.
In a pot add 8-10 pieces of dry amla, 2 tsp chai patti, 1.5 cups water, and boil for sourness.
In a pressure cooker, heat 2 tbsp oil and add whole spices: 2 black cardamom, 1 inch dalchini, 3-4 cloves, 1 green cardamom, 1/2 tsp black pepper.
Add the onion-anardana paste to the spices and sauté, then add salt to taste.
Cook until pressure cooker releases pressure naturally after 5 to 6 whistles then simmer for 10 minutes before opening.
Add 1/2 tsp ginger-garlic paste and sauté for 1 minute, then add 2 medium tomatoes pureed.
Add 2 tsp chole masala, 1/2 tsp yellow chilli powder, 1/2 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp dhania powder, 1/2 tsp jeera powder and cook the masala for 2 minutes until oil shines.
Add soaked chole (without soaking water), 1/4 tsp meetha soda, peeled raw potato, and strained amla-tea water mixture to the cooker.
Add 1.5 to 2 cups water and cook on high flame with pressure cooker lid until 5 to 6 whistles, then low flame for 10 minutes, then let pressure release naturally.
Mash the potato in the cooked chole mixture if desired and boil the chole further on high flame for 10 to 15 minutes to thicken the gravy.
Prepare tempering by heating ghee and adding 1 inch ginger juliennes and 1/4 tsp ajwain, sauté for 15-20 seconds and pour over chole.
Divide the rested dough into 10 medium-sized balls.
Press each dough ball gently for 10 minutes to relax tension before rolling and optionally apply a light touch of flour if needed.
Roll out each dough ball like a puri with no cracks and fry immediately in hot oil until puffed and golden, flipping once to ensure even puffing.
Serve hot bhature with prepared chole.
